preamble: Rhotacism of the voiceless alveolar stop [t] to the alveolar trill [r]. In Hausa, Klingenheben's law turned syllable-final t into the rolled ř (*fátkée > fářkée 'itinerant trader'). In the Saharan languages, Proto-Saharan *t corresponds to r in Kanuri and Teda-Daza (*tu 'to see' > Kanuri rú). Intervocalic tapping of /t/ to [ɾ], as in North American English, is filed under t → ɾ.

examples.note: Klingenheben's law (coronal rule): a syllable-final coronal stop becomes a rolled r
In the clipped form the t becomes syllable-final

Proto-Saharan reconstructions are Cyffer's (2020, Oxford Handbook of African Languages) as tabulated on Wikipedia. The homophonous demonstrative *tu 'that' keeps t (Kanuri túdu, Teda-Daza te̥ye), so the change is not general in initial position.
Final *t surfaces as r before an added vowel; Beria ʊ́gʊ́rī also has r.

sources: Newman, P. (2004). Klingenheben's Law in Hausa. Rüdiger Köppe. https://lccn.loc.gov/2005390185
